resolved.rationale: Reviewer B claims: High Severity - Potential ID Space Exhaustion
Reviewer B claims: File: tsdb/head.go
Reviewer B claims: Lines: 2865-2868

Reviewer B claims: Description: The panic check for chunk ID space exhaustion (>= oooChunkIDMask-1) is good, but there's no recovery mechanism. In a long-running system, this could cause crashes. Consider adding a way to gracefully handle this case (e.g., forcing compaction).
Reviewer B claims: Medium Severity - Documentation Inconsistency
Reviewer B claims: File: tsdb/chunks/chunks.go
Reviewer B claims: Lines: 76-100

Reviewer B claims: Description: The documentation was simplified but lost some important details about chunk ID allocation behavior. The new docs don't clearly explain the relationship between firstChunkID and mmappedChunks/headChunks.
Reviewer B claims: Low Severity - Test Coverage Gap
Reviewer B claims: File: tsdb/head_read_test.go
Reviewer B claims: Lines: 501-575

Reviewer B claims: Description: The new test TestMemSeries_chunk_ResolveAfterWrap is good but doesn't cover the case where both in-order and OOO chunks wrap simultaneously. Consider adding a combined test case.
Reviewer B claims: Low Severity - Potential Integer Overflow
Reviewer B claims: File: tsdb/head_read.go
Reviewer B claims: Lines: 403-423

Reviewer B claims: Description: While wrapChunkID handles modulo arithmetic, there's no explicit check for integer overflow when firstChunkID grows very large. The current implementation relies on pushHeadChunk's panic check.
Reviewer B claims: Performance Impact
Reviewer B claims: The new wrapChunkID operations add a small overhead to chunk ID calculations. While negligible for individual operations, this could add up in high-throughput scenarios.
Reviewer B claims: Maintenance Complexity
Reviewer B claims: The chunk ID wrapping logic adds cognitive overhead when debugging chunk-related issues. The test cases help, but the behavior is non-intuitive when IDs wrap around.
Reviewer B claims: Backward Compatibility
Reviewer B claims: The changes assume all existing systems will properly handle wrapped chunk IDs. While the tests verify this, there may be edge cases in older systems that assumed monotonic IDs.
